scope: Definitions retained outside the visible interface.
dnase_display: ln(1 + mean original K562.bw signal per genomic bin)
description_html:
About the comparison

Metrics compare clipped predictions with clipped targets in the visible region, using the same bounds. MSE is divided by (maximum − minimum)²; RMSE is its square root. Pearson uses those same clipped values. Each supported bin pair is counted once, including the diagonal.

Choose Explore maps to browse all chromosomes, or Compare predictions to see the matching trained target, baseline and neural output. Overfit predictions cover 32 selected chr3/chr4 regions and their subdivisions. These regions were used for fitting. Here, the observed target and distance + DNase baseline match the selected model’s training target. Zero counts with positive expectation retain the model’s lower-bound label. Undefined expectations and unavailable inputs stay masked.

Elsewhere, the Viewer shows the original observed maps and the historical baseline in log-count units. A prediction is not invented for an untrained region or transform. Cross-transform baseline accuracy is not reported. Raw-reference colors do not affect comparison metrics.

DNase: Each panel uses your measured K562.bw, averaged within each bin. Incomplete coverage is missing. DNase is always displayed as ln(1 + mean K562.bw signal), with no scale selector.

Panel profiles (map units): Each genomic bin is averaged across its supported partners in that panel’s full map, after the displayed clipping. The raw panel uses its own raw color bounds. The other three panels use identical bounds and common support. Actual diagonal cells contribute once per row; supported zeros and zero-derived lower-bound labels remain included. Gray lines in the baseline and prediction panels show the observed target for direct comparison. Shared profile axes preserve amplitude differences; no per-profile rescaling or smoothing is applied. Profiles follow the horizontal genomic axis. Zooming selects the part of these full-window profiles to display. “1D PCC” compares the visible native-bin profiles and is separate from the contact-map metrics.

Relation to the Hi-TrAC paper: cLoops2 get1DSig extends each PET endpoint by ±50 bp, adds the basewise coverage and divides by twice the library’s unique PET count, then multiplies by one million. The new observed HiTrAC track sums raw PET ends per map bin and divides by bin width in kb. Actual diagonal PETs contribute two ends. It uses supported contacts with both endpoints in the complete source window, independently of heatmap normalization or clipping. It is binned coverage, not exact cLoops2 RPM: the .hic does not retain within-bin endpoint positions or the matching cLoops2 library metadata. The same measured track appears beneath every panel. Separately, each panel’s map profile summarizes that panel’s clipped values. Clipping removes information needed to recover exact PET counts, so predicted RPM is not inferred. Sources: Hi-TrAC paper and cLoops2 1D plotting.
